description: House style for the post-conversion refactor pass: how to reshape an already-correct, auto-generated pandas pipeline for readability WITHOUT changing behavior. Consolidate imports, extract helpers, group exports at the end, and tidy comments.

imports_at_top.title: Consolidate every import at the top of the file, de-duplicated and grouped.
rule: Move all `import`/`from ... import` statements to the top of the file.
Remove duplicate imports (auto-generated code often repeats `import pandas as pd`).
Order the block: standard library, then third-party (pandas, numpy, sklearn), then local (`import metadata as md`).
Keep `import metadata as md` -- the pipeline reads and writes datasets through it.
pitfalls: Do not drop an import that is still used further down; run a mental check that every name is still imported.

extract_helpers.title: Replace repeated logic with small, well-named helper functions.
rule: When the same transform repeats across steps, factor it into one helper and call it each time.
Give helpers a clear verb-based name (`add_running_total`, `winsorize`, `join_lookup`) and a one-line docstring.
Keep helpers pure where possible: take a DataFrame (and params) in, return a DataFrame out.
Do not over-abstract: a transform used only once should stay inline.
pitfalls: Extracting a helper that mutates its argument in place can change behavior for a later step that reuses the original frame -- copy inside the helper or return a new frame.

code: def add_scaled(df: pd.DataFrame, col: str, factor: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
"""Return a copy of df with `col` multiplied by `factor`."""

exports_at_end.title: Group the export calls near the end, in finalization order.
rule: Collect the `md.export_data(df, name)` calls together near the end of the script, ordered by when each dataset is finalized.
The SET of exported dataset names must stay EXACTLY the same -- never rename, add, or drop an export.
EXCEPTION: if a later section re-imports a dataset via `md.import_data(name)`, that dataset must be exported BEFORE the read; correctness beats grouping.
pitfalls: Deferring an export past a later `md.import_data` of the same name makes the read fail or read stale data -- keep such an export before its consumer.

tidy_comments.title: Keep one short comment per logical section; remove noise.
rule: Add a brief section comment describing WHAT each block does (e.g. `# --- build customer features ---`).
Delete redundant comments that merely restate the code (`# add 1 to x`).
Prefer clear variable and helper names over explanatory comments.
A short module docstring summarizing the pipeline is welcome but optional.
pitfalls: Do not remove a comment that records a non-obvious business rule or a SAS quirk being reproduced.
